content: The text provided appears to be a detailed and technical description of various studies, search strategies, and methodologies related to pharmaceutical pricing, reimbursement policies, and procurement practices across different countries and contexts. 1. Moïse P and Docteur E conducted an in-depth analysis of pharmaceutical pricing and reimbursement policies in Mexico, providing insights into the mechanisms and challenges faced in this region. 2. Garattini L, Van de Vooren K, and Freemantle N explored the application of tendering and value-based pricing strategies in Italy, specifically focusing on human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines. Their findings highlight lessons learned from the Italian healthcare system. 3. The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) published a comprehensive report on pharmaceutical pricing policies in a global market, emphasizing the economic and social implications of these strategies. 4. Ackermann A, Reinaud F, Ando G, and Izmirlieva M evaluated the impact of the 2011 German healthcare reform on pharmaceutical prices, shedding light on the economic outcomes of policy changes. 5. Fedyaev D, Fedyaeva V, and Omelyanovskiy V analyzed government procurement practices for medicines used in the treatment of rare diseases in Russia, providing a critical assessment of the system's efficiency and equity. 6. Van Haeren E, Arickx F, Soete E, Bormans V, Mortier M, and Leveque F examined public tendering for off-patent pharmaceuticals in Belgium, using the case of simvastatin to illustrate the effects of competitive procurement on pricing. 7. Alabbadi I and Hammad EA investigated the impact of generic drug entry and price competition in Jordan's public health sector, highlighting the economic benefits and challenges associated with increased market competition. 8. Hornyák L, Nagy Z, Ilku L, Tálos Z, Endrei D, Ágoston I, et al. studied the pricing competition and reimbursement policies for biosimilar granulocyte-colony stimulating factors in Hungary, offering insights into the cost-effectiveness of biosimilars. 9. Petrou P and Talias MA analyzed the use of tendering as a reimbursement tool for pharmaceuticals in the Cyprus public health sector, discussing its implications for cost containment and access to medicines. 10. Yin T and Jiang B assessed the effects of drug procurement under a cap price policy in Sanming, China, providing evidence of its impact on drug affordability and availability. 11. Dutta A and Bandyopadhyay S explored whether policy interventions aimed at improving access to medicines work equally for poor and non-poor populations, using a comparative approach to assess equity in healthcare. 12. Hay CRM discussed the procurement of factor concentrates through competitive tendering in the 21st century, focusing on the implications for hemophilia treatment. 13. Casanova-Juanes J, Mestre-Ferrandiz J, and Espin-Balbino J compared the national reference pricing system with the regional tendering system for outpatient prescription medicines in Andalusia, Spain, analyzing their effects on market competition and pricing. 14. Vogler S, Gombocz M, and Zimmermann N reviewed tendering practices for off-patent outpatient medicines in Belgium, Denmark, and the Netherlands, identifying key lessons from these countries' experiences. 15. Curto S, Ghislandi S, Van de Vooren K, Duranti S, and Garattini L conducted an empirical analysis of regional tenders for biosimilars in Italy, focusing on the awarded prices and their implications for healthcare budgets. 16. Danzon P, Mulcahy A, and Towse A examined pharmaceutical pricing in emerging markets, analyzing the effects of income levels, market competition, and procurement practices on drug prices. 17. Petrou P investigated the long-term effects of tendering on the prices of branded pharmaceutical products, providing evidence of sustained cost reductions. 18. Qendri V, Bogaards JA, and Berkhof J studied the pricing of HPV vaccines in European tender-based settings, highlighting the role of competition in achieving cost savings. 19. Wouters OJ, Sandberg DM, Pillay A, and Kanavos PG analyzed the impact of pharmaceutical tendering on prices and market concentration in South Africa over a 14-year period, providing a longitudinal perspective on procurement practices. 20. Adesina A, Wirtz VJ, and Dratler S reviewed the reform of antiretroviral price negotiations and public procurement in Mexico, discussing the outcomes and challenges of these policy changes. 21. Barbosa K de S and Fiuza E examined the effects of demand aggregation and credit risk in pooled procurement, using evidence from Brazilian public purchases of pharmaceuticals and medical supplies. 22. Newman KL, Varkey J, Rykowski J, and Mohan A conducted a quasi-experimental study on the impact of providing antibiotic cost data to prescribers, analyzing its effect on the prescription of high-cost antibiotics in an academic and tertiary care hospital. 23. The search strategies employed in the studies utilized advanced filters and indexing systems, such as MeSH headings, to identify relevant records on pharmaceutical pricing, reimbursement mechanisms, and procurement policies. These strategies were designed to balance sensitivity and specificity, ensuring comprehensive coverage of the literature. 24. The retrieved records were systematically reviewed, deduplicated, and assessed for relevance, with a focus on identifying key themes and trends in drug pricing and policy research.
